title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed in a scenario their battery capacity had not been engineered to handle. When heavy traffic from Fourth of July celebrations created prolonged gridlock near the Golden Gate Bridge, multiple vehicles exhausted their batteries while stuck in standstill conditions and required towing. The company attributes this to unanticipated congestion and road closures rather than a system malfunction.

This is a failure of operational design rather than a model or software error. Autonomous vehicles need to either maintain sufficient battery reserve for foreseeable traffic conditions in their deployment zone, or have a strategy for the situation they cannot operate their way out of. The system was used in conditions it had not been prepared for, and catching this would have required either better traffic modeling during peak events or different battery assumptions before launch.

It is not established whether Waymo had been warned of the scale of Fourth of July traffic, or whether similar vehicles in manual operation were similarly affected. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, but the relationship between this incident and the battery failures is unclear.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo driverless vehicles ran out of battery power and required towing after becoming stuck in heavy traffic during Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco. At least a dozen autonomous cars, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined the streets following a fireworks display near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the gridlock to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unexpected road closures. Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to improve its vehicles' resilience during severe congestion.

Passengers and other motorists reported frustration with the stranded vehicles, with one driver spending nearly two hours in standstill traffic. One Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries occurred. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss the incident with public and private partners to prevent similar traffic problems in the future. This incident follows a December incident when Waymo vehicles stalled during a city-wide power outage.
